audit.whatIsWrong: The page invents a 'percent-HP passive' for K'Sante in five places (whys[0], whys[5], whys[6], late, wants.foe[1]). Dauntless Instinct marks targets to take MORE DAMAGE ON HIS NEXT ATTACK — no percent health anywhere. It also credits Q with a knockup (the knockback and stun are Path Maker; two Ntofo stacks fire a shockwave that PULLS) and calls Path Maker a 'block' (it is charge-up damage reduction that then dashes, and it deals true damage).
audit.why: Advice built on a percent-health passive tells a player to build HP against a champion whose real threat is a marked auto plus true damage from Path Maker — the exactly wrong itemisation read.
audit.corrected: Percent-HP claim removed everywhere it appears in the edits; Ntofo Strikes stated as a 450-range slow, 3.5s, 20 mana, with the two-stack pull; Path Maker as charge-through-damage into a stun; All Out's wall knockback flagged as the reason to hold Flash for the terrain, and its healing flagged for Grievous Wounds.

edits.after: Overload reaches 1000 but Ntofo Strikes is a 450-range slow he re-casts every 3.5 seconds for 20 mana — with no root and no Flux loop yet, farm the level out and take nothing for free.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are his sustained advantage window. His Heartsteel stacks mean every trade you attempt feeds his scaling, his W block eats one of your combo hits outright, and All Out can be popped the moment you overextend. Play the wave: push Flux through minions to rack up poke damage without entering his engage range, use Teleport or Realm Warp at 6 to find value elsewhere rather than forcing a 1v1 you lose on cooldown math. The one genuine lever is Phase Rush — if he blows All Out on an open-lane all-in, proc Phase Rush on the first hit and walk backward through the wave; his duelist form is immobile enough that the speed boost actually buys you the few seconds you need for cooldowns to reset.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 are his sustained advantage window. Heartsteel stacks mean every trade feeds his scaling, Path Maker charges through your damage before it dashes in to stun, and All Out can be popped the moment you overextend — its knockback launches you through a wall, so hold Flash for the terrain rather than the damage. Play the wave: push Flux through minions for chip without entering his 600 range, and at 6 spend Teleport or Realm Warp on value elsewhere instead of a 1v1 you lose on cooldown math. The one genuine lever is Phase Rush — if he spends All Out on an open-lane all-in, proc it on the first hit and walk back through the wave; the speed buys the seconds your cooldowns need.

edits.before: Two completed mana items is your honest power window. Your Flux cascade sustains damage through his resists, your CDR keeps W and E on near-zero downtime, and Realm Warp turns you into a teamfight carry who never has to win the 1v1 he was always going to dominate. Side-lane against him only in short burst trades — E a minion, root, empowered Q, Phase Rush out — never the extended brawl where his percent-HP passive compounds. Let your team collapse the map while you warp the fights he can not follow.

notes: The 'percent-HP passive' on this page is fabricated — Dauntless Instinct marks targets to take more damage on K'Sante's next attack. It appeared in five places and pushed the reader toward the wrong itemisation. Q was credited with a knockup; the knockback and stun belong to Path Maker, and two Ntofo stacks PULL. Path Maker also deals true damage, so stacking resistances is the wrong answer (recorded, not written, for want of room). Level chart rows 1 and 6 flipped in matched pairs per the mirror.
